quotes.text: Pubmed, 2022. URL https://huggingface.co/datasets/ncbi/pubmed

rationale: Sources (PubMed case reports, MedQA, college materials) are named with a platform and a 2022 PubMed snapshot year, and the data are on Hugging Face. No explicit route from a task to its source record is stated, so the score is 1 rather than 2.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
The data are released under a credentialed-access data use agreement

rationale: Origin, collection (routine care, generation pipeline), data-use terms (DUA) and consent status (review board waiver of consent) are all stated. Note that this S1 sentence conflicts with the paper's other statements that the vignettes come from public PubMed case reports.

quotes.text: against the U.S. adult inpatient population reported in a national hospital discharge survey

rationale: Age, sex and race distributions are compared with a named target population (U.S. adult inpatient population per a national hospital discharge survey), with differences under five percentage points.

searched: S1 (paper and appendices), S2 (no chunks), S3 (no chunks), S5 (no chunks). S1 has no dedicated unsafe-output or bias test. The safety and bias suites appear only in an S4 code comment (agent_eval/notes.py), which never counts as reporting under G1a.

quotes.text: A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.
Manual review of the top 10% of cases ranked by either similarity metric revealed no exact matches with the original publications.

rationale: Developer-side controls (held-out private split, canary string) are stated in S1, and a measured check is reported (sentence-completion memorisation test in Appendix C.1 with BLEURT/ROUGE results). Note that S1 elsewhere says both the full and curated datasets are public on Hugging Face.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: S1 states that the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time and names the mechanism (separate evaluation service, no network path, labels unpublished).

quotes.text: Our experiments use gpt-4.1 with temperature = 0 as the backbone for

rationale: The dataset is released and fixed, but the evaluation depends on a live gpt-4.1 API call for the LLM mapper and parser with no snapshot or version pin. Software and the simulator are not pinned, so 1.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct.

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for every task, and the result is reported (all 120 graded correct).

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: The packet states that the grader checks unchanged state as well as changed state, so out-of-scope modifications are detected. NA does not apply because the packet describes graded state changes.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate is reported, and per-metric chance rates are said to be in the appendix.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: A random agent's score is reported over tasks in S1 (3.1%). An S4 comment gives different figures (2.5% random, 0.0% do-nothing) but S4 never counts as reporting; the numeric discrepancy is noted, not flagged as a contradiction.

quotes.text: We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: The benchmark validates its own grader and mapper with figures (false-accept 1%, false-reject 2%; mapper precision and recall in Table 6; kappa 0.655 on 50 cases).

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: Temperature 0, a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy are stated in S1. Note that the Limitations section says only a single run was done per model, and F.3 mentions eight runs, which is internally inconsistent.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: S1 reports 95% bootstrap CIs for all model scores and a paired permutation test for the difference between the two best models.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: A run count per task (three) and seed/temperature policy are stated; independence of runs is not stated. The run count is inconsistent with the single run in Limitations and the eight runs in F.3.

quotes.text: so the resampling unit is the task; where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs are reported, the resampling unit is named (task, or patient when tasks share a patient), and clustering within patients is addressed.

quotes.text: each task executed eight times. We report pass^8 (share of tasks solved in all 8 runs)

rationale: A pass^8 all-runs metric and final-state agreement across eight runs are reported with the run count. Action-sequence agreement is not shown.

quotes.text: Grok 3 mini beta, February 2025.
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed

rationale: Model references carry release or access dates, and temperature 0 with a fixed seed is stated for all runs. No harness tag or commit is stated as matching the reported numbers, and no provider snapshot IDs are given.

quotes.text: Tools are specified using JSON schemas with name, arguments, and types.
Agent prompts include these tool descriptions.

rationale: JSON schemas for tools, read/modify-state documentation per tool, and return values including errors are stated. The paper says agent prompts include the tool descriptions, so (ii) reaches the agent-visible surface; S5 has no chunks to confirm it directly.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.
Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses

rationale: Conformance tests are reported, stubbed tools are disclosed, and the paper states the disclosure is in the tool descriptions shown to the agent. S5 has no chunks, so the S5 reach rests on the paper's own statement.

quotes.text: Once you order any lab or imaging investigations, you can no longer gather additional history or perform examinations on the patient
which was simulated by our evaluation framework
(2) excessive or inappropriate investigation ordering

rationale: Investigation orders are clinical orders that lock further history and examination, they are simulated by the examiner, and excessive ordering is a scored failure mode (investigation precision, relevance requirement for accuracy). The reproduced agent system prompt does not say orders are simulated, so S5 reach is false.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: Grader input is end state, so a non-state rationale is not needed (element ii counted as vacuously met). Validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates is reported.

quotes.text: Web access is blocked during runs; retrieval is confined to the task environment, preventing answer leakage through search.
A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.
Released tasks include a canary string.

rationale: Web and retrieval leakage controls, a private held-out split absent from public surfaces, and a canary string are all stated. Note that S1 elsewhere says the full and curated datasets are public on Hugging Face.

quotes.text: Subgroup analysis demonstrated variation in model performance across different specialty groups
Endocrine & Reproductive (150), Infectious Disease & Immunology (150)

rationale: Results are reported per specialty group with group sizes given in Appendix C. The schema holds demographics (age, gender, ethnicity) but no per-patient-subgroup results are reported.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
The data are released under a credentialed-access data use agreement

rationale: Records are stated as real de-identified, with a DUA and review-board waiver. S1 does not state data terms separately from a code licence; that appears only in an S4 comment, which does not count. This S1 sentence also conflicts with the paper's public PubMed sourcing.
